extractor_note: types parsed with the TypeScript compiler API; router.go with group-prefix resolution

methodology.key: `METHOD /openapi/path/template`. A frontend call whose shape matches no contract operation keeps its resolved literal path; a URL expression this extractor cannot resolve is listed in unknown_entries instead of being guessed.
rulings: `command_id` is only asked of the methods that change state (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE); `n/a` means the method does not change state, `unknown` means the backend does not register it so no idempotency contract exists, and only a registered state-changing route with no Idempotency-Key on the call site reads `no`.

`retry: fallback_mock` is reserved for a src/mocks answer behind import.meta.env.DEV; a hard-coded fallback that answers a *failed request* in production is `fallback_static` and is called out separately because the plan forbids it in production.
`project_scope` is path-based. A project id carried only as a query filter or a request-body field is `global` - migrating such a call is not a scope change.

`orphan_client` is a frontend call to a path the backend never registered; `contract_only` is a contract+router endpoint nobody calls, and `backend_unregistered` is a contract operation the router never registers - the three are different facts and are never merged.

`legacy_only` vs `legacy_unused`: both mean only the old client calls it. The difference is whether any production code - another old client included - still calls that client module. Only `legacy_unused` is dead code; `legacy_only` means T12.03.b has a caller to rewrite first. `legacy_direct` covers a path called through the shared transport with no client module at all - nothing to delete there.

auth/envelope/command_id are read off the call site source (regex over the enclosing statement plus the AST shape); each row carries a `check_notes` line naming the evidence, and a call site with no readable evidence reads `unknown` rather than a guess.

sources.callers: every .ts/.tsx under apps/workbench is parsed with the TypeScript AST. An import binding is followed (aliases, namespace imports, default-object imports, dynamic import() and re-export chains included) and a module counts as imported whenever the imported name is evaluated as a value in that file: called, passed (`useQuery({ queryFn: f })`, `onClick={f}`), spread, or returned. Type-only positions never count. Anything the walker cannot attribute goes to `unresolved_imports` and its endpoint is never reported as caller-free.
sources.clients: apps/workbench/services/** is the old client layer; apps/workbench/src/services-bridge/** is the bridge; apps/workbench/api.ts is the shared transport both import helpers from.
sources.generated_types: apps/workbench/generated/openapi-types.ts: OpenApiOperationMap is read back to tie the endpoint to the generator contract.
sources.openapi: backend/docs/openapi.yaml: operation set, experimental flag, response content types.
sources.router: backend/internal/api/router.go: group aliases resolve to full prefixes, `:param` normalizes to `{param}`, the handler name is the registered function.

schema_coverage.method: openapi.yaml is walked as parsed YAML; generated/openapi-types.ts is walked with the TypeScript AST. The two counters are independent populations - a mismatch is reported as a fact, and this script never edits the generator.

mismatches.why: the contract marks 5 schemas `nullable: true`; the generated file writes `| null` for 4 of them and collapses the fifth (`LiteralValue.@value`, which has no `type:`) to `unknown`, so one nullable site loses its null at the consumer boundary.

the contract counts every name in a `required:` list anywhere in the document (including query/path parameters); the generated file emits one non-optional member per property of an exported object schema, so parameter-level requireds have no generated member to land on.

the contract counts `enum:` members in every schema; the generator emits a literal union per enum property and skips boolean-like literals, so reused or nested enums are emitted once per use and the member counts diverge.

a pagination parameter is a query parameter in the contract and a property of whichever generated schema models that response, so names overlap without being the same population (only `limit` and `after` appear as generated properties).
